question: True or false: when a patient consults a GP about a headache, the chance it comes from a brain tumour is about 1 in 100?
answer: False. It is ten times smaller. Using UK primary care records of 3,505 brain tumour patients and 17,173 controls, Hamilton and Kernick put the risk behind a headache consultation at 0.09%, about 1 in 1,100. Headache is common and brain tumours rare, so tumour headaches sit among thousands of ordinary ones. New neurological signs shift the odds far more.
move: A sign common in a rare disease can still say almost nothing alone.
trap: True, because headache is the textbook first sign of a tumour.
source: Hamilton & Kernick, Br J Gen Pract, 2007
